text:
Nothing about the Hurricanes' start needs an asterisk. They are 13-3-2, project to about 114 points, and our simulations give them a 74% chance at the Metropolitan Division. The goals, 69 for and 42 against, match the chances almost exactly: 59.25% of the expected goals (the quality of chances both ways), 58% at 5-on-5.

The depth is the point. Sebastian Aho and Andrei Svechnikov with William Carrier have taken 66% of the expected goals in their minutes. Nikolaj Ehlers, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake have been better still, 71% and a 9-0 goal edge. Stankoven has 12 points in his last 10. Both top pairs on the blue line are at 55% or better.

Pyotr Kochetkov has added a hot stretch on top: .945 and 6.9 goals saved above expected over five starts. That's the part to expect less of.

The story underneath: Mark Jankowski has been filling in for Jordan Staal, which Cory Lavalette wrote up for The Athletic, and has seven points in 10. Lavalette also reported Staal on the ice for Saturday's morning skate. When he's back, a team that already wins the chances gets one more center to throw at people.
headline: Carolina is the real thing
